fields.meta_title: Landing Page SEO: Build One Page per Query | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Landing page SEO in seven steps, with launch checks from Google's own tools and a builder that hands you the page as code. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build Landing Page SEO Into Code You Own, Tag by Tag
fields.hero_description: Describe the offer and the query it should answer. Emergent builds the page and its lead form as code you own, with the title tag and schema you specify.
fields.features_heading: What Goes Into an SEO Landing Page
fields.features_subheading: Landing page SEO is the work of ranking one page for the query its buyers search, then turning some of that traffic into leads.
fields.feature_1:
Title tag and H1 written around the query

Your prompt names the query, and the title tag, H1 and slug are worded the way buyers type it. When Search Console shows impressions but few clicks, a follow-up prompt rewords it.
fields.feature_2:
Sections in the order searchers need them

Emergent lays out the H2s around the questions your buyers ask next, in the order you list them. The lead form goes where you place it: under the opening section or at the end.
fields.feature_3:
Structured data and canonical tags

SoftwareApplication, LocalBusiness or BreadcrumbList markup goes into the page as JSON-LD when your prompt lists the type. A canonical URL and a sitemap entry go in on request too.
fields.feature_4:
Speed findings you can fix by prompt

PageSpeed Insights reports Core Web Vitals for the published page on mobile and desktop. Paste a finding, such as an oversized hero image, into the chat and Emergent fixes the code.
fields.feature_5:
Leads saved with their landing URL

Submissions land in a database you own, tagged with the landing URL and referrer you ask the form to record. Organic leads stay apart from paid, and HubSpot or Slack can get a copy.
fields.feature_6:
Markup you can audit and keep

Export the page, form included, to your GitHub repository as plain code. A developer can check every tag with the crawler they use, and the page moves hosts with no rebuild.

fields.usecase_heading: SEO Landing Pages for Four Kinds of Query
fields.tab_content_1:
One feature page for one buying query

Northwind sells shift scheduling software, and that phrase is what its buyers search. The prompt puts it in the title tag, H1 and URL, with SoftwareApplication markup for the product. Demo requests land in a table with the landing URL attached.
fields.tab_content_2:
Four branches with copy of their own

A moving company has crews in four Colorado cities, and they do different work. Downtown high-rises lead the Denver page; Boulder's is about student moves. LocalBusiness markup on every page carries the branch address. Quote requests post to the Slack channel of the branch they came from.
fields.tab_content_3:
What a fair comparison table shows

A rival's strengths stay in the table. The Acme vs Globex page keeps the mobile app row, where Globex is ahead. BreadcrumbList markup places the page under Compare, and the feature pages it mentions are linked from the bottom.
fields.tab_content_4:
The template preview comes before the email field

Nothing is gated until the visitor has seen the content calendar template: a preview of the sheet and short notes on filling it in. Maya at Lumen enters her work email and the file downloads. Her new HubSpot contact lists this page as the source.

fields.howto_title: How to Build an SEO Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Start from one query and the pages already ranking for it. Build the page to that standard, then judge it by the leads it brings in, not by traffic alone.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Match what the top results deliver
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Answer before you ask for anything
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose the single query the page should rank for and check that the top results are pages like yours. If the first page of Google is all guides, a sales page will struggle there; write a guide-shaped page or pick another query.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open the top ten and note what they have in common: format, length, whether they show prices, which questions their H2s cover. Match the format, then cover the questions they skip. That gap is what the page adds.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write a title tag that leads with the query and differs from every other title on the site. Use the same wording in the H1 and keep the URL short. The meta description summarizes this page in a sentence or two, not the brand.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Open with a plain answer to the query in the first two lines, then cover the topic at the depth the search needs. The form goes after that answer, never above it, and asks only for what you will use.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick the structured data that fits the page: SoftwareApplication for a software feature page, LocalBusiness for a branch, BreadcrumbList for pages deep in the site. Link to the new page from related pages, with anchor text that names its topic.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test the page on a phone
fields.howto_step_6_des: Load the page on a mid-range phone and run it through PageSpeed Insights. Compress the hero image and give it a width and height. Defer any script the first screen does not need, and fix layout shift before you publish.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish on your domain and add the URL to your sitemap. Once a week, compare the query's impressions in Search Console with its clicks and form conversions. A page with clicks but no conversions needs work on the offer, not the SEO.

og.headline: Build landing page SEO into code you own, tag by tag
og.alt: Build landing page SEO into code you own, tag by tag, with Emergent

scope.evidence: Meta title 'Landing Page SEO: How to Build Pages That Rank', H1 'Build Landing Page SEO Into Pages That Rank and Convert' and hero 'Name the query and describe the offer...' cover ranking plus conversion, the whole job; no sibling topic. (Outcome wording of 'Pages That Rank' is judged under truth.)

intent.evidence: Top 10 is guides (Semrush, Search Engine Land, Coalition, MailerLite, Instapage blog) plus builders (Unbounce, Landingi, Zoho). Page carries a definition (FAQ 1 'Landing page SEO is the practice of getting one landing page to rank...'), a 7-step how-to ('01 Pick one query per page' ... '07 Publish, then measure each week'), a checklist answer and four page types, then the builder offer. Both PAA on-topic items answered ('How do you optimize landing pages?', 'Does Wix offer landing pages?').

specificity.evidence: Cycle-1 fix confirmed: table cell now 'Prompt for the page and its on-page SEO' (seo variant). Examples are concrete and unglamorous: 'shift scheduling software', 'movers in Denver', '/movers/fort-collins', 'Acme vs Globex', 'content calendar template', 'URL Inspection in Search Console'.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence with a verb: 'A feature page targets one commercial query...', 'Choose the single query the page should rank for...', 'Export the page and its lead form...'. The shared shape of those openers is a voice problem, scored under voice.

craft.evidence: Tacked-on or summary clauses (CONTENT_DEFECTS #4): (1) tab_content_2 'Prompt for a page per branch, each with its own H1, service area and LocalBusiness schema, and no two pages read alike.' The last clause has no subject link to the prompt and also repeats the H3 'each with its own copy' ('each with its own' twice in one tab). (2) howto_step_4_des ends on a summary restating 'Put the form after that answer': 'Visitors and crawlers should both reach the content before they reach the ask.' (3) tab_content_4 '...each lead is stored with its source page while the contact is created in HubSpot.' ('while' clause bolted on; split into two sentences). (4) faq_10 closes on an aphorism: 'In search, the homepage tends to rank for the brand name, while each landing page ranks for the problem it solves.'

voice.evidence: Templated rhythm (HUB_RULES 2b 'no run of sentences starting the same way', 'same rhythm paragraph after paragraph'). A. Prompt-imperative openers, every instance: hero_description 'Name the query and describe the offer.'; feature_1 'Name the query in your prompt and Emergent writes...'; feature_2 'Tell Emergent what the searcher came for...' + 'Prompt for the lead form below the first answer.'; feature_3 'Ask for Product or LocalBusiness schema...' + 'Name a canonical URL and a sitemap entry in the same prompt...'; feature_4 'Ask for a responsive layout...'; feature_5 'Ask for the form to save...'; tab_content_1 'Prompt for the query in the title tag, H1 and URL...'; tab_content_2 'Prompt for a page per branch...'; tab_content_3 'Ask for the differences in a table...'; tab_content_4 'Ask for an email before the download...'; features_heading 'What to Ask for in an SEO Landing Page'; meta_description 'then prompt Emergent for...'. 13 prompt imperatives in 12 short fields; 5 of 6 features open this way, and the hero plus features 1 and 3 share the exact '[Imperative], and Emergent [verb]s' shape. Fix: state the SEO behaviour once as prompt-driven (hero or features_subheading), then let most features open on the result ('The title tag and H1 carry the query you name...', 'Product or LocalBusiness schema goes in as JSON-LD when the prompt asks') and vary the rest. B. All four tabs follow one three-beat template: definition opener ('A feature page targets one commercial query, such as...', 'City pages target searches like...', 'Comparison pages answer queries like...', 'Template pages target queries like...'), then 'Prompt for/Ask for...', then a lead-saved closer ('Each demo request is saved with its landing URL.', 'Quote requests are saved with the city attached...', 'The trial signup at the end records which comparison...', 'each lead is stored with its source page...'); the four tab H3s are also all imperatives ('Aim...', 'Publish...', 'Answer...', 'Turn...'). Vary at least two tabs' structure. C. Repeated device: 'one more prompt' in feature_1 ('one more prompt rewords the title') and feature_4 ('Each issue it flags is one more prompt to fix'). D. 'each' 27 times across 15 fields (e.g. features_subheading 'each organic visit', feature_5 'each submission', tab_content_1 'Each demo request', tab_content_2 'each with its own' x2, tab_content_4 'each lead', faq_6 'each follow-up question', faq_7 'one type and one query each', faq_9 'each one', faq_10 'each landing page', howto_step_7 'Each week'); cut at least half. E. Tidy triplets: feature_6 'Run any crawler against it, hand it to a developer, or host it elsewhere'; faq_4 'Thin copy, duplicate pages and a stray noindex tag'; howto_description 'Write the page..., check it on a phone..., and judge it by the leads'.

truth.evidence: (1) faq_9 'Keep campaign duplicates and test variants out of the index with a noindex tag': Google's A/B testing guidance is rel=canonical to the original for test variants, not noindex; fix to 'point test variants at the original with a canonical tag'. (2) tab_content_3 'Ask for the differences in a table with Breadcrumb schema': Breadcrumb schema describes the page's position in the site, not a table; the sentence says the table carries it. Fix: 'Ask for the differences in a table, Breadcrumb schema on the page, and links to...'. (3) features_subheading '...and turning each organic visit into a lead': no page converts every visit; say 'turning organic visits into leads'. (4) Outcome promise against the 'no ranking promise' brief: h1 'Build Landing Page SEO Into Pages That Rank and Convert' (and share_image alt / OG title repeating it) states ranking as what Emergent builds; consider 'Build an SEO Landing Page That Converts Organic Traffic' or similar, keeping the meta title's how-to framing. (5) P2: feature_3 and howto_step_5_des recommend 'Product' schema for a software feature page ('Product for a feature page'); for SaaS, SoftwareApplication is the type Google documents; say 'Product or SoftwareApplication'. Cycle-1 truth fixes verified: no 'Each page gets a canonical tag', no 'responsive from the first build', no 'scripts load after the content', no 'Indexed' badge (cover and OG now 'Page published'), no 'teaches more than most courses' or AI-summary generalization; SEO behaviour is framed as prompted throughout (feature_3 'Name a canonical URL and a sitemap entry in the same prompt, and both go in'). Claims map to claims_used (prompt-build, api-connect for HubSpot/Slack, code-export, database-owned, custom-domain, free-start). Table is library-generated (V2/V3 clean); Wix K7 pending with Divit, not scored.

distinct.evidence: Organised by query type ('Feature Pages', 'City Pages', 'Comparison Pages', 'Template Pages') and on-page SEO steps; nothing shared with thank-you-page beyond the FAQ link ('along with every thank you page'). PPC is split off in faq_4 ('For pages that only take paid clicks, build a PPC landing page instead') and local business in faq_7 ('For a single storefront or office, start with a local business landing page'). P2 watch: tab 2 'City Pages' (LocalBusiness schema, movers in Denver) sits close to the planned local-business-landing-page; keep that tab about multi-location query targeting when the sibling is written.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic items, sources recorded, drift removed (cycle-1 fix verified: salary/learn-SEO items gone), each answered in its first sentence. Fails CONTENT_DEFECTS #18 (an FAQ answer that restates the body), every instance: faq_2 'starts with one query per page and a format that matches the results already ranking for it' = howto steps 01 'Pick one query per page' and 02 'Match what the top results deliver'; 'a query-led title tag and H1, an answer up top' = step 03/04. faq_5 'a single query, placed first in the title tag and again in the H1' = howto_step_3_des 'Lead the title tag with the query... repeat it in the H1'; 'answers that query in its first two lines' = howto_step_4_des 'a plain answer in the first two lines'; 'Every image has alt text' = howto_step_5_des 'Give every image descriptive alt text'. faq_8 'Give every image a width and height to stop layout shift' = howto_step_6_des 'set its dimensions... fix layout shift' and feature_4 'fixed image sizes'. faq_6 'Open with an H1 that holds the query and a two-line answer' = mockup 'open with a two-line answer' and step 04. The same 'answer first' idea appears in 12 fields ('answer' 18 times: faq_1, faq_2, faq_5, faq_6, faq_8, feature_2, howto_step_2_des, howto_step_4_des, tab_content_1, tab_content_3, mockup). Fix: make faq_2 answer the PAA with what the steps don't cover (internal link anchors, refreshing an existing page, what Emergent adds) and keep faq_5 to the check-before-launch items not in the how-to (Rich Results Test, URL Inspection, inbound links); cut the dimension advice from faq_8 or from step 06. Plus the faq_9 noindex error under truth. Links pending with Divit (ppc, local business not yet live) not scored.

images.evidence: Each tab shows one moment matching its copy: tab 1 checklist 'Query in the title tag / H1 / URL / Demo request form' and 'Demo request saved, Landing URL attached'; tab 2 '#aurora-branch', 'City: Aurora', 'LocalBusiness schema, On every city page'; tab 3 'Read: Acme vs Globex', 'Breadcrumb schema', chips 'Scheduling / Reporting / Payroll' matching the mockup's feature pages; tab 4 'Source: content calendar page', 'Contact created in HubSpot'. Cursor on button edges, panels full, cover 'Page published' (cycle-1 'Indexed' fixed); tab 1 email now 'dana@pinecrest.co' (cycle-1 note fixed). P2 notes: tab 4 'Download link emailed to Maya' is not in the tab copy ('Ask for an email before the download'); tab 2 H1s 'Movers in Denver/Boulder/Aurora/Fort Collins' are the city-swapped pattern the copy says to avoid ('no two pages read alike'), so vary one.

plan.angle: The top 10 is guides (Semrush, Search Engine Land, Instapage, MailerLite) plus builders (Unbounce, Landingi, Zoho). The page wins by being the guide an operator can act on: a seven-step method checked against Google Search Central, launch checks with Google's own tools, and four query types shown as real pages, with Emergent as the builder that hands over the code instead of an SEO settings panel. No ranking promise anywhere.
